messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Dedicated pool 'crestline-prod' experiencing sustained GPU queueing. Tenant: CrestlineCorp. Metrics: pool GPU util 90%+, avg queue 47 reqs >30s. Severity: page. Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-gpu-pressure.

maya (oncall): I'm on it, joining the call.

kevin (sre): Looking at Grafana -> https://grafana.internal/r/dedicated/crestline-prod (cpu/gpu/queue). Spike started ~12:07 UTC. 92% of queued requests attributed to tenant crestlinecorp. No OOMs, just queueing.

liam (eng-ml): Crestline is hitting the model 'gpt-large' with many long-seq requests (avg seq ~900). We have a quantized variant 'gpt-large-q4' that uses less memory and gives ~1.6x throughput. Options: burst from shared pool OR route heavy sequences to q4.

sara (csm): CSM here. Crestline is seeing production 503s/timeouts on autocomplete in production. They've asked for immediate mitigation. Their contract includes emergency burst credits (up to 2x for up to 60m).

ella (ops): If we enable burst, what's the cross-tenant risk? We need to avoid evicting other paying customers.

kevin (sre): Risk: burst will draw from shared burst capacity. We can cap at 2x for 60m per contract to limit exposure. Alternative is tenant throttling to reduce concurrency. Proposal: combine burst + throttle + model-downgrade.

maya (oncall): Proposed plan (vote):
1) Enable emergency burst for crestline-prod for 60m with 2x cap.
2) Apply per-tenant concurrency throttle to 70% of usual.
3) Route seq>512 requests to 'gpt-large-q4' via routing transform (canary 5% -> 100%).
4) Monitor for 10m stabilization then escalate if not improved.

liam (eng-ml): I can push the routing transform and spin up q4 replicas. ETA ~6m for canary. I'll instrument a canary metric.

kevin (sre): I'll run the burst command. Command: `infractl burst enable --pool crestline-prod --tenant crestlinecorp --duration 60m --cap 2x`

maya (oncall): Go for it. Paging the triage group: @kevin (sre) @liam (eng-ml) @sara (csm)

incident-bot: Command acknowledged: infractl job queued. Provisioning additional capacity.

kevin (sre): Burst toggle executed: provisioning +88 GPUs to crestline-prod pool. Observing queue length dropping from 47 -> 12 in first 90s. GPU util trending down to ~72%.

liam (eng-ml): Routing config pushed: canary at 5% -> now 5% of heavy seq traffic hitting gpt-large-q4. Logs: `service-router: reroute applied for tenant=crestlinecorp sequence>512 -> model=gpt-large-q4`.

sara (csm): Notified Crestline support: "We've enabled emergency burst and routing changes; please avoid running large batch experiments for the next 60m." They acknowledged.

maya (oncall): 12:18 UTC: 503s dropped by 95%, median latency back to SLO. Continuing to monitor. If GPU queue >20 OR util >85% for 10m, re-escalate.

ella (ops): Note: please add billing flag for emergency burst usage. CSM to follow up with billing notes.

kevin (sre): Will tag the infra event with `billing:crestline-emergency-burst` and create incident ticket #INC-2789123456.

maya (oncall): Handoff prep: I'll be handing to dennis (night oncall) in 30m. Current state: burst active, throttle 70%, q4 routing at 100% for seq>512 after successful canary. Stabilized.

dennis (oncall-night): Ack, I'll take over at 12:50 UTC. Escalation triggers I have: queue >20 for 10m, GPU util >85% for 10m, or customer reporting >1% error rate.

kevin (sre): Plan for scale-down: auto-schedule deallocation at T+60m. If metrics stay healthy for 20m prior to end, we'll scale down early and remove throttle.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Burst capacity deallocation scheduled at +60m from 2789123456.

kevin (sre): Deallocation executed at T+54m early after sustained stability. Pool GPUs returned to baseline. Final metrics: avg queue <3, gpu util ~45%, errors back to baseline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Dedicated pool crestline-prod capacity pressure mitigated. Postmortem owner: kevin (sre). Follow-ups: ["Automate suggestion to route long-seq traffic to q4 variant","Add detection rule to recommend throttle+burst pairing","CSM to reconcile billing for emergency burst"]. Ticket: #INC-2789123456

maya (oncall): Thanks team — good ops. Closing handoff thread.

sara (csm): Will open a customer post-incident note and schedule a sync with CrestlineCorp to discuss sustained mitigation (pre-warming models / request shaping).

kevin (sre): I'll own the postmortem and schedule the 1-hour retro.

maya (oncall): closing thread. :white_check_mark:
